Therefore, per dating correspondences derived from ''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'', ''Andor'' Season 2 begins in [[4 BBY]] and ends in [[1 BBY]]. |preceded by=[[Andor Season 1|''Andor'' Season 1]] |followed by= }} {{Quote|If we do not stand together, we will be crushed.|Mon Mothma|{{SW|url=news/swce-2023-lucasfilm-studio-showcase|text=SWCE 2023: 11 Highlights from Lucasfilm's Studio Showcase}}}} '''''Andor'' Season 2''', alternatively titled '''''Andor: A Star Wars Story'' Season 2''', is the second and final season of the television series ''[[Star Wars: Andor]]'', comprised of twelve episodes. It was already in pre-production by [[May]] [[2022]] and started production on [[November 21]], 2022;{{WebCite|url=https://collider.com/andor-season-2-filming|text=Here's When 'Andor' Season 2 Starts Filming [Exclusive]|date=2022-11-04|work=[[Wikipedia:Collider (website)|''Collider'']]|archivedate=20221104211108}} it was set for release in [[2024]],{{WebCite|url=https://collider.com/andor-season-2-timeline-explained|text=Tony Gilroy Reveals When 'Andor' Season 2 Begins|author=Maggie Lovitt|date=2022-11-23|work=[[Wikipedia:Collider (website)|''Collider'']]|archivedate=20241209162943}} but was later confirmed to release in [[2025]] starting on [[April 22]], 2025. While [[Andor Season 1|Season 1]] took place entirely in [[5 BBY]], Season 2 takes place over the course of four [[Standard year|year]]s. Separated into four three-episode blocks, each showing a few days of a year, the final block leads into the [[Mission to the Ring of Kafrene|opening scene]] of the film ''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]'',{{WebCite|url=https://www.fandom.com/articles/andor-finale-season-1-spoilers-2|text=‘Andor’ Creator Talks Season 1 Finale Spoilers and Where Season 2 Will Go|author=Eric Goldman|date=2022-11-23|work=[[Wikipedia:Fandom (website)|Fandom.com]] {{C|Articles}}|archivedate=20241009160311}}{{BookCite|author=Ryan, Mike|container=Andor Season 2|title=[[Wikipedia:Empire (magazine)|''Empire'']]|number=January 2025|publisher=[[Wikipedia:Bauer Media Group|Bauer Media Group]]|date=2024-11-21|pages=pp. 49-53}} which is set in [[1 BBY]]. ==Official synopsis== ''Cassian Andor continues the path toward his heroic rebel destiny.'' ==Official description== ''Lucasfilm’s Emmy®-winning thriller “Andor,” returns for its long-awaited conclusion [on April 23]. The second season takes place as the horizon of war draws near and Cassian becomes a key player in the Rebel Alliance. Everyone will be tested and, as the stakes rise, the betrayals, sacrifices and conflicting agendas will become profound. Rife with political intrigue and danger, the series is a prequel to “Rogue One: A Star Wars Story,” which portrayed a heroic band of rebels who steal the plans to the Empire’s weapon of mass destruction—The Death Star—setting the stage for the events of the original 1977 film. “Andor” sets the clock back five years from the events of “Rogue One” to tell the story of the film’s hero, Cassian Andor, and his transformation from disinterested, cynical nobody into a rebel hero on his way to an epic destiny.''{{Disney|subdomain=press|domain=co.uk|url=press-kit/andor-season-2-press-kit|text=Andor Season Two Press Kit}} ==Official alternative description== ''Rife with political intrigue, danger, tension, and high stakes, “Andor” is a prequel to “Rogue One: A Star Wars Story", which portrayed a heroic band of rebels who steal the plans to the Empire’s weapon of mass destruction: The Death Star, setting the stage for the events of the original 1977 film. “Andor” sets the clock back five years from the events of “Rogue One” to tell the story of the film’s hero, Cassian Andor, and his transformation from disinterested, cynical nobody into a rebel hero on his way to an epic destiny.'' ''Andor Season 2 will see the characters and their relationships intensify as the horizon of war draws near and Cassian becomes a key player in the Rebel Alliance. Everyone will be tested and, as the stakes rise, the betrayals, sacrifices and conflicting agendas will become profound.'' ==Development== [[File:AndorS2Pitch-AndorZine.png|thumb|left|200px|The pitch for ''Andor'' Season Two dated to December of 2022]] {{Quote|No one goes in a revolution if it's not for love, for a real need of bringing change for a community. ''[…]'' It's a love story. There's no revolution without love.|Diego Luna, on ''Andor''|{{YouTube|channel=heyuguysblog|name=HeyUGuys|video=a_KQmQpalgY|text=Andor Season 2 - Revolution Needs Passion: Love Fuels Change|date=2025-04-11}}}} According to writer [[Tony Gilroy]], the plot of ''Andor'' was based on historical revolutions.{{WebCite|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/tv/0/tony-gilroy-interview-andor-star-wars-disney-plus|text=Andor creator Tony Gilroy: ‘My Star Wars characters are based more on Trotsky than Trump’|author=Stephen Armstrong|date=2025-04-23|work=[[Wikipedia:The Daily Telegraph|''The Telegraph'']]|archivedate=20250423093955}} [[Diego Luna]], who played Cassian Andor, said in an interview in [[April 11]], 2025 that revolutions are based on love. [[Elizabeth Dulau]], who played Kleya Marki, said in an interview published on [[April 28]] that beneath the rigid veneer of her character was "a lot of love" that motivated her to sacrifice her daily life for the rebellion.{{WebCite|url=https://vogue.sg/elizabeth-dulau-kleya-marki-andor-season-2|text=“The rebellion is her entire life”: Elizabeth Dulau on playing Kleya Marki in ‘Andor’ Season 2|author=Azrin Tan|date=2025-04-28|work=[[Wikipedia:Vogue Singapore|''Vogue Singapore'']]|archivedate=20250428122249}} Gilroy said that he used historical revolutions as a catalog for fictional stories, with a focus on exploring the behavioral aspect of individuals—such as what they fear or the banal selfishness of agents of the state—and integrating them with the journey of a character like Cassian Andor waking up to political consciousness. Among the early work he did for ''Andor'' was figuring out what ideal futures would characters have in mind following their revolution, but Gilroy deliberately left any discussion of the future out of Season 2 because the characters would be too busy fighting the Empire.{{YouTube|video=SUUw-UfK64Q|text=Andor, Trump and Our Revolutionary Times | The Weekly Show with Jon Stewart|channel=@WeeklyShowPodcast|name=The Weekly Show with Jon Stewart|date=2025-07-10}} According to Gilroy, a litany of historical events therefore informed his story in ''Andor'', such as the Soviet revolutionaries [[Wikipedia:Leon Trotsky|Leon Trotsky]] and [[Wikipedia:Joseph Stalin|Joseph Stalin]] who [[Wikipedia:1907 Tiflis bank robbery|robbed a bank]] to fund the revolution, or the French Resistance comprising [[Wikipedia:Charles de Gaulle|Gaullists]], Communists, and the [[Wikipedia:Maquis (World War II)|Maquis]] who hated each other. A part of ''Andor'' Season 2 was filmed at the [[Wikipedia:City of Arts and Sciences|City of Arts and Sciences]] complex in [[Wikipedia:Valencia|Valencia]].{{WebCite|url=https://vogue.sg/elizabeth-dulau-kleya-marki-andor-season-2|text=“The rebellion is her entire life”: Elizabeth Dulau on playing Kleya Marki in ‘Andor’ Season 2|author=Azrin Tan|date=2025-04-28|work=[[Wikipedia:Vogue Singapore|''Vogue Singapore'']]|archivedate=20250428122249}} According to [[Michael Wilkinson]], around 4,045 costumes were created for the second season.{{Instagram|username=michaelwilkinson|url=stories/michaelwilkinson/3683246582855845882|name=Michael Wilkinson|date=2025-07-24|quote=At a rough count, for Season 2, we made about 3,050 costumes for Extras, 715 costumes for Principal Cast, 115 costumes for Creatures and about 165 costumes for Stunts – so all in all, about 4,045 costumes! We had 4 workrooms in-house at Pinewood studios in London – Men’s cast, Women’s cast, Secondary cast and Crowd – and then we also had outside workrooms making costumes for us when we ran out of room! For Andor Season 1, we made over 3,000 costumes.|nolive=1|archive_blocked=1|archivefile=File:MichaelWilkinson-TotalCostumeCount-Instagram.png}} ==Release and reception== Season 2's trailer, released in February 2025, uses [[Wikipedia:Steve Earle|Steve Earle's]] [[2004]] [[Wikipedia:Cowpunk|country punk]] song [[Wikipedia:The Revolution Starts Now (album)|''The Revolution Starts Now'']],{{SWYouTube|AE4wxt70aUM|Andor | Season 2 Trailer | Streaming April 22 on Disney+}} which addresses how citizens ought to actively defend American [[democracy]] in light of the [[Wikipedia:2004 United States elections|election]] and ongoing [[Wikipedia:Iraq War|war in Iraq]] that year.Liner notes of [[Wikipedia:The Revolution Starts Now (album)|''The Revolution Starts Now'']] — {{WebCite|url=https://www.steveearle.net/discography/revolution.php|text=The Revolution Starts…Now|work=[https://www.steveearle.net SteveEarle.net]|archivedate=20241201170414}} In an interview with [[Wikipedia:The Daily Telegraph|''The Telegraph'']] published on [[April 23]], 2025, Tony Gilroy was asked if there was any order from Lucasfilm to "adjust the depiction of the Empire in light of a presidency that could be seen to mirror it" in light of Donald Trump's [[Wikipedia:Second presidency of Donald Trump|second term]] as US President. Gilroy replied that he would be asking the same question if he was in the interviewer's place but elaborated that his story and characters were based on historical revolutions. In an interview conducted ahead of Season 2's premiere and published on [[May 13]], [[Wikipedia:Variety (magazine)|''Variety'']] asked Gilroy about motifs of unrest across ''Andor'', noting how the series "summons images of [[Wikipedia:Russo-Ukrainian War|Ukraine]], [[Wikipedia:Gaza war|Gaza]], [[Wikipedia:Fall of Kabul (2021)|Kabul]] and [[Wikipedia:2019–2020 Hong Kong protests|Hong Kong]]" of current affairs "alongside references to the French Revolution, [[Wikipedia:Oliver Cromwell|Oliver Cromwell]] and Nazi propaganda" in past history—Gilroy said that he was writing about all revolutions and insurrections and how he felt that people, including himself, often have a narcissistic and individualistic belief that they are living in a unique time of history despite that not being "the pattern of history." Nevertheless, seeing audiences draw current real-world parallels to the series, such as a sense of authoritarianism threatening democracies like the United States, is a reflection on "if people find history knocking at their door, there's probably all kinds of places they can look for references."{{WebCite|url=https://variety.com/2025/tv/news/andor-finale-diego-luna-tony-gilroy-star-wars-1236394652|text=Andor Finale: Diego Luna, Tony Gilroy on Revolutionizing 'Star Wars'|author=Adam B. Vary|date=2025-05-13|work=[[Wikipedia:Variety (magazine)|''Variety'']]|archivedate=20250513161511}} On the same day, Gilroy said during a livestream on the official ''Star Wars'' YouTube channel that fascism not only destroys the people that the ideology is used to target but also the people who enact it, referring to [[Dedra Meero]] and [[Syril Karn]].{{SWYouTube|uvkpcedAtXs|Andor Season 2 with Diego Luna and Tony Gilroy LIVE | Now Streaming on Disney+}} Dedra Meero's actor, [[Denise Gough]], expressed in interviews her belief that artists like herself using their platforms to speak up for the Palestinian people is important to keep up a groundswell of support through democracies like Ireland for the rights of other people.{{YouTube|video=_omQdodjg_M|text=‘Andor’ Star: I Refuse to Stay Silent on Gaza|channel=@BreakThroughNews|name=BreakThrough News|date=2025-05-31}} When asked about including the word "genocide" in a ''Star Wars'' series at the ATX TV Festival of [[May 29]]–[[June 1]], Gilroy expressed that it is sad that many people could find an immediate emotional resonance with the word; ''Andor'' writer [[Beau Willimon]] mentioned he also found that people could find the series motivating for their own actions, with Gilroy adding to the cheers of the audience that Willimon himself has made personal sacrifices as president of the [[Wikipedia:Writers Guild of America, East|Writers Guild of America, East]].{{YouTube|video=FMOw6gP4r7Q|text=ANDOR with Tony Gilroy & Beau Willimon | ATX TV Festival|channel=@ATXTV|name=ATX TV|date=2025-06-10}} In [[Wikipedia:Ross Douthat|Ross Douthat's]] interview of Gilroy for [[Wikipedia:The New York Times|''The New York Times'']] that was published on [[June 5]], the two discussed how ''Andor'' focused on the destruction of community and the future of AI. Gilroy said he had discussed AI with people in [[Wikipedia:Los Angeles|Los Angeles]] in the past few days and came across the "terrifying" prospect of a [[Wikipedia:AI alignment|misaligned]] AI superintelligence killing all humans arriving as early as [[2027]], or alternative dystopic scenarios such as mass unemployment and an AI nuclear race between the United States and China.{{WebCite|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/06/05/opinion/film-hollywood-andor-politics.html|text=What Makes Art ‘Left Wing’?|author=[[Wikipedia:Ross Douthat|Ross Douthat]]|date=2025-06-05|work=[[Wikipedia:The New York Times|''The New York Times'']]|archivedate=20250606092427}} In a podcast recorded with the host [[Wikipedia:Jon Stewart|Jon Stewart]] and historian [[Wikipedia:Mike Duncan (podcaster)|Mike Duncan]] on [[July 9]], Gilroy discussed his use of historical revolutions and how he realized overcoming a common obstacle like the Galactic Empire or the Russian tsarist regime took precedent for the people directly involved, ahead of any discussion on a desired future after the fight and without a common goal. Duncan agreed and added that a common feature of revolutions is that they start with ideals and slogans such as freedom and democracy but spiral out of any individual's control, and once they had successfully removed a regime, authority, sovereignty, and legitimacy had to be [[Wikipedia:Constructivism (international relations)|reconstructed]] and inevitably lead to the movement's splintering, allowing the influence of power-seeking figures such as Lenin to dominate.{{YouTube|video=SUUw-UfK64Q|text=Andor, Trump and Our Revolutionary Times | The Weekly Show with Jon Stewart|channel=@WeeklyShowPodcast|name=The Weekly Show with Jon Stewart|date=2025-07-10}} In the same vein, Gilroy said he had adapted the "authoritarian playbook" of "building the enemy you want," giving the examples of [[Wikipedia:J. Edgar Hoover|J. Edgar Hoover]] with the civil rights and anti-war movements, the British state with the [[Wikipedia:Provisional Irish Republican Army|IRA]], or [[Wikipedia:Benjamin Netanyahu|Benjamin Netanyahu]] with [[Wikipedia:Hamas|Hamas]], complementing the spontaneous nature of uprisings, such as the [[Wikipedia:Tunisian revolution|martyr]] of the Arab Spring. The podcasters then discussed the US seemingly becoming a "tinderbox." Gilroy had thought about some of the audiences' remarks that ''Andor'' has been "predictive" of America in the past six months, with the mineral rights over Ghorman echoing the US' ambitions over [[Wikipedia:Greenland|Greenland]], the migrantion issue on [[Mina-Rau]] echoing the US [[Wikipedia:United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement|Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE)]] agency's [[Wikipedia:Deportation in the second presidency of Donald Trump|hardline deportation operations]], and the [[Arrest of Dasi Oran|arrest]] of Senator Dasi Oran in the Senate Building echoing US Senator [[Wikipedia:Alex Padilla|Alex Padilla]] being forcibly detained at a federal press conference. Gilroy added he was surprised a confrontation over an ICE raid had not yet led to an event akin to the [[Wikipedia:Kent State shootings|Kent State shootings]] during the anti-war protests in 1970 and prompted a declaration of martial law, and he suggested a civil conflict would then perhaps be a desired outcome for the "tech right" like [[Wikipedia:Peter Thiel|Peter Thiel]] of [[Wikipedia:Palantir Technologies|Palantir Technologies]] who are using Trump as a "host organism" and, as expressed in the interview with Ross Douthat on [[June 26]], would not care if AI wipes out humanity. Gilroy recalled that the fantasy author [[Wikipedia:J. R. R. Tolkien|J. R. R. Tolkien]] disliked allegories and pointed out that they are different from applicability—Gilroy realized that the audience of ''Andor'' have found the story applicable to many different contexts. Although he was hesitant, especially at the start of Season 2's press tour, to let interviewers associate political labels with ''Andor'', he has felt sadness as people around the world find ''Andor'' resonating deeply with their own experiences. The podcast speakers nevertheless expressed hope that the series, having become part of contemporary popular culture, could help people adapt to the changing times. ==Media== {{Mediacat|from=1|imagecat=Images from Andor Season 2}} ===Episodes=== {| {{Prettytable}} !
